data.long_meaning: From the Greek word igeneia, meaning 'strong, firm, or obedient'. In Greek mythology, Igenia was a virgin priestess of Hera, the goddess of marriage and childbirth. She was the daughter of King Pelias and was eventually sacrificed to appease the gods. Her story is a tragic reminder of the importance of obedience and faith.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of unwavering faith and obedience.
data.etymology: Igenia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong, Firm.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Igenia total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
data.cultural_impact: The name "Igenia" has a rich cultural background in Greek mythology. It is a powerful name that conveys strength and obedience. In ancient times, Igenia was revered as a virgin priestess of Hera, the goddess of marriage and childbirth. Her name reflects the values of purity and devotion to the gods.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Igenia" holds a significant spiritual meaning as it reminds us of the importance of faith, obedience, and sacrifice in our lives. In Greek mythology, Igenia was a loyal and obedient daughter who sacrificed herself to appease the gods. Her story serves as a reminder of the power of obedience and unwavering faith, even in the face of sacrifice.
